intro.summary: St Scholastica was a 6th-century Benedictine nun and sister of St Benedict, remembered for her life of prayer and monastic devotion.

blocks.title: Introduction

blocks.notes: expanded canonical prayer references into full rosary texts; Adjusted line breaks for clearer spoken pacing, and placed the personal-intention marker on its own line.; converted "mention request here" into a personal-intention pause marker; reused compacted prayer source from an earlier section; converted intention marker into sacred bell and personal-intention pause

parts.text: In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. O God, Thou caused the soul of Thy blessed virgin Scholastica to enter heaven in the form of a dove, to show us the way of innocence. Grant us, by her prayers and merits, to live in such innocence, that we may deserve to attain eternal joys. Through Jesus Christ, Thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end. Amen. Saint Scholastica prayed in love and confidence. Because of her love, her prayer was heard and answered. Through her intercession, let us now pray: V. By the example and intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, keep us faithful to Thy word. R. Hear us, O Lord. V. By the example and intercession of St Scholastica, keep us rooted in Thy love. R. Hear us, O Lord. V. By the example and intercession of all the holy virgins, keep us firm in prayer and charity. R. Hear us, O Lord.

Lord our God, Thou robed the virgin St Scholastica with the beauty and splendor of love. Help us to walk blamelessly before Thee so that in the company of virgins we may praise Thy Name for ever, and find our delight in Thee, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen. Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. St Scholastica, pray for us! In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
